transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Noah Rivera (Redwood Solutions Eng); Dr. Sara Voss (Amberline CTO), Miguel Ortega (Platform Lead), Priya Sharma (Security), Ethan Cole (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Amberline is evaluating Dedicated capacity for PHI workloads and wants isolation + KMS integration. Primary drivers: predictable p95 latency for clinical-document-generation inference, data residency in EU, and strong audit logs. They have sharp bursts (cron-driven nightly batch + marketing spikes) and want pre-warm strategy plus fallbacks to hosted. Security wants details on HSM/KMS and audit retention.

Topics covered:
- Dedicated vs hosted failover and fallback policies
- Pre-warm / hot pool sizing and warm-up latency
- Encryption at rest / KMS / HSM integration and key rotation
- Isolation / tenant fencing and blast-radius mitigation
- Benchmark plan (50k token warm-run, 72-hour soak)
- Compliance scope (HIPAA/European data residency)

Questions (flagged during call):
- Can Dedicated nodes be tied to a customer-managed KMS? - yes/no and how
- What's the billing model during burst (reserved + burst on-demand)?
- How quickly can Redwood failover to hosted in an outage?

Transcript body:
00:00 - Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, i run AE for the bio vertical. Today with me is Liam, our SE, and noah in solutions. How's everybody doing?
00:08 - Dr. Sara Voss: Good, thanks. We wanted to get into the nuts and bolts — we're trying to decide between hosted and a dedicated reservation for our inference workloads. A big one is PHI and encryption.
00:18 - Miguel Ortega: Yeah hi, i'm Miguel. Quick context: we push a nightly clinical report job that creates a big burst around 02:00 UTC, and we also get user-driven spikes during business hours. Our p95 latency target for document gen is 700ms right now, cost is also a concern.
00:33 - Liam Chen: okay, cool. So you're looking at two constraints: isolation/compliance for PHI and also predictable latency for that nightly batch and interactive spikes. Can you tell us the typical concurrency during the nightly job and the interactive qps?
00:45 - Miguel Ortega: Nightly job is parallelized across ~120 workers, each worker calls inference roughly 40 times in a 10-minute window. Interactive is more spiky, average 15qps with peaks to 120qps.
01:02 - Ethan Cole: i want to add we have a policy that any PHI must be encrypted in a customer-controlled KMS and keys rotated every 90 days. Also audit logs need 1 year retention.
01:12 - Noah Rivera: got it. So a couple of points: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools which we can pin to region EU-West and enable a customer-managed KMS integration. There is a small infra handshake to set up HSM-backed keys if required.
01:27 - Priya Sharma: how does the KMS integration actually work? does the model or runtime ever see plaintext keys? we need assurance that keys are never exported.
01:37 - Liam Chen: good question. The integration is via our KMS connector — Redwood never stores key material, calls to unwrap/decrypt are proxied, and for HSM we can do an attestation flow. i'll drop a one-pager on the flow. (inaudible)
01:51 - Dr. Sara Voss: we also have to consider blast radius. If one tenant spikes, we need tenant fencing; pre-warmed nodes for the nightly job can't be affected by other customers' churn.
02:02 - Maya Patel: absolutely. For Dedicated we can do either strict physical isolation or strongly isolated multi-tenant routing with tenant fencing. For a regulated bucket like PHI we usually recommend single-tenant nodes or VPC private deployment.
02:16 - Miguel Ortega: what about bursting? We don't want to pay for 100% capacity all the time. ideally reserve baseline for the nightly workload and allow burst to hosted or on-demand nodes during peaks.
02:28 - Liam Chen: that's a common pattern. We have a hybrid runway: reserved dedicated pool for baseline + automatic burst to compatible hosted instances. The controls let you set per-route fallbacks and cost thresholds. In practice, we've seen customers reserve ~30-50% of peak and allow burst for the rest.
02:45 - Ethan Cole: how quick is the burst? if we overflow into hosted, do we see warm-up latency penalties? i.e., do tokens have to rebuild KV cache?
02:53 - Noah Rivera: yes, transitions can cause cold starts for KV cache. We do prefix caching and some KV snapshot warmers, but you should expect some latency tail for the first few minutes when moving traffic to a new variant. That's why pre-warm or warm-pools are important.
03:10 - Dr. Sara Voss: can we talk numbers? our p95 is 700ms target. what commit level would you recommend? how many GPUs?
03:20 - Liam Chen: we'd want to run a quick capacity model. very roughly, for the model you mentioned, on A100-equivalent (quantized) we estimate X requests/s per GPU at your prompt lengths. We'll run an exact benchmark with your prompt set. For sizing, the nightly batch pattern suggests reserving enough capacity to handle the 120 workers * 40 calls with headroom; that maps to N GPUs — we'll provide a workbook.
03:43 - Miguel Ortega: please, send the workbook. Another bit: our infra team insists on SOC2 + offline audit logs and API-level audit events for all inference calls. retention one year as noted.
03:55 - Maya Patel: Redwood supports SOC2, and we can enable extended audit retention for Dedicated. We also offer per-request metadata logging and export hooks to your SIEM. i'll include the SOC2 certificate and audit process doc.
04:06 - Priya Sharma: for key rotation, any downtime or rekey window? we want zero-downtime rotation ideally.
04:12 - Liam Chen: typically rotation is seamless if you use a KMS that supports decrypt with new keys and a key alias swap. For HSM-backed solutions we recommend a short-key handover window but we can coordinate. we'll put in runbooks.
04:25 - Dr. Sara Voss: alright, what about cost modelling — we need examples for 100k tokens/day vs 1M tokens/day with different reserve levels.
04:33 - Maya Patel: we'll share a pricing matrix with reserved rates, burst on-demand rates, and an example cost projection spreadsheet. we also include amortized pre-warm costs and warm-pool hours.
04:44 - Ethan Cole: one operational question: network egress — does dedicated in EU have different egress fees? we need to model that too.
04:50 - Noah Rivera: egress follows cloud-region norms; we'll call out expected egress and a couple of patterns customers use to mitigate costs (e.g., batching responses, smaller embeddings).
04:59 - Miguel Ortega: benchmarks — we can provide a canonical prompt set, but expect some typos in the transcripts i mean prompts will vary. we still want a 72-hour soak after you sign to validate sustained behaviour.
05:13 - Liam Chen: that's reasonable. Our SE team can run a 50k token warm benchmark within a few days and then scale to a 72-hour soak once we agree on pilot scope. we'll need your prompt set and a traffic curve.
05:25 - Priya Sharma: what about data residency? we can't let PHI leave EU. if Redwood must failover to hosted for burst, can that be restricted to EU-region hosts only?
05:34 - Maya Patel: yes, region-restricted failover is supported — we can configure routing policies to only route to EU-hosted variants. If absolute residency is required, then private on-prem or VPC private deployment is the recommendation.
05:47 - Dr. Sara Voss: timeline: we want to move quickly — ideally pilot in 3 weeks, procurement in 6-8 weeks. Are those realistic?
05:55 - Maya Patel: pilot in 3 weeks is reasonable if we get the prompt set and traffic histograms this week. procurement timelines vary; for Dedicated and customer-managed KMS there is a security review that usually takes 4-6 weeks.
06:08 - Miguel Ortega: okay let's recap next steps.
06:11 - Maya Patel: recap: (1) Redwood sends pricing + SOC2/KMS one-pager, (2) SE runs 50k token benchmark with prompt set, (3) Amberline shares traffic histograms and key rotation policy, (4) schedule follow-up deep dive with KMS engineer next Wed.
06:28 - Dr. Sara Voss: perfect. Thank you everyone.
06:31 - Maya Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up with links.
